sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri Prashant Singh, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Durg Vijay Singh, learned Additional Advocate General assisted by Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.
This is the second bail application on behalf of the applicant.
The first one was rejected by this Court vide order dated 22.8.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.21812 of 2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.21812 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 4. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.129 of 2014, under Sections 376(3), 506 IPC and 3/4 (2) POCSO Act, Police Station Medical, District Meerut with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that as a new ground, it is the period of incarceration on which the applicant is entitled for bail as he is in jail since 04.04.2024 and more than one year and four months have passed since his incarceration.
During trial, three witnesses have been examined and the other witnesses are formal witnesses only.
Eleven more witnesses remain to be examined, as such, there is no likelihood of conclusion of trial in near future.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that there is no question of applicant tampering with evidence.
He is not a flight risk, as such, he is entitled for bail.
Earlier on this Court had directed expeditious trial of the instant case, but the trial is moving at a snail's pace.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that there is likelihood of early conclusion of trial.

8. The Supreme Court in case of X vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the trial being almost at its logical end and there being no new ground for pressing the second bail application, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.

The bail application is found devoid of merits and Atul vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84935264/
2 is, accordingly, rejected.

entities.text: Atul vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

(Krishan Pahal,J.) September 4, 2025 (Ravi Kant)
